intro.title: Engineering Loops
intro.sub: Prompt, context, harness, loop. Four ways to steer an AI, and each one wraps the last in a bigger loop. Focus a ring, or take the tour from the center out.

diagram.loopCaption: the open-ended outer loop: no fixed "done". self-triggered, self-verifying, self-improving. inner loops terminate, this one doesn't.
diagram.contextUnbroken: edits code that was never broken
diagram.schedulerLabel: a trigger starts the run: no human turn
diagram.loopProblem: harness alone: idle until a human prompts, · cold-starts every run
diagram.loopSupervisorRole: sets policy once, then steps out

layers.title: Prompt Engineering
layers.tagline: a loop you run by hand.
layers.hook: Just tell it what to do.
layers.definition: You shape the words. Give it a role, break the task into steps, add an example, ask it to think out loud. One instruction goes in, one answer comes back. The whole craft is phrasing.
layers.insight: A perfectly worded prompt still can't hand the model facts it never received. Phrasing alone runs out of road.
layers.caption: "just tell it what to do"

points: They're sharp, but they know nothing about your world
So how you word the ask is everything
Say it vaguely and you get a confident wrong answer

layers.title: Context Engineering
layers.hook: Give it what it needs to know.
layers.definition: Now you curate everything the model sees before it answers: chat history, retrieved docs, tool output, live state. The prompt becomes one stream inside a much richer context. The agent even starts reading files and calling tools to gather that context itself.
layers.insight: There is only so much room. Pack in too much and a long task fills the context window and chokes.
layers.caption: reads files, calls tools

analogy.lead: Like handing someone the right case file.
points: Same sharp person, but now they hold the documents
The answer is only as good as what's in the folder
Make the folder too thick and they lose the thread

layers.title: Harness Engineering
layers.guidanceNote: you design it, the agent runs inside it
layers.hook: Build the world it runs in.
layers.definition: Everything around the agent except the model itself. Agent equals model plus harness. You give it real tools, a sandboxed worktree, memory on disk, and a task list it works one item at a time into a fresh context. Verifiers like tests and type checks feed results back so it can self-correct.
layers.insight: Most "prompt failures" in production are really harness failures. Fix the scaffolding, not the wording.
layers.caption: one task at a time, into a fresh context

analogy.lead: Like a workshop, not just a worker.
points: A bench, the right tools, notes on the wall, a checklist
The room is what makes the work reliable
Swap the worker and the room still holds

layers.title: Loop Engineering
layers.hook: Set a goal, let it run.
layers.definition: Now you put the harness in motion. Give it a goal and a stopping rule, then let it cycle: reason, act, check the result, decide, repeat. A scheduler wakes it on its own. It grows itself with new skills, spins up subagents to check its work, and runs jobs in parallel.
layers.insight: You stop being the person in the chat box and become the person who builds the machine that runs it.
layers.caption: goal → act → check → repeat

analogy.lead: Like hiring a team, not doing the task.
points: You set the goal and the guardrails
The team runs the cycle without you in the room
You review the result, not every keystroke

chart.title: One shot gets you partway. A loop gets you further, faster.
chart.sub: Quality against attempt number: you checking in yourself versus the loop checking itself on every single pass.
chart.takeaway: A self-checking loop climbs faster and lands higher, because it catches its own misses instead of waiting for you to.

closing: prompt → context → harness → loop · each ring adds a loop around the last
